headline: Without AI-related companies, US shares have gained about 5.5% this year, slightly less than Europe's 5.6%, according to a Yahoo Finance analysis.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: the full article was read; it matches the headline, but it is an analysis built on an index whose AI-related names are not listed.
importance_line: What changed is a clear estimate of how much of America's stock-market lead this year comes from AI, which matters first to savers whose funds are heavy in US shares, then to European economies that capture less of the AI spending, then to the AI companies lifting the US index, and the doubt is that the comparison depends on how the index defines "AI-related", which the article does not set out, and the article itself says AI is not the whole story behind the US lead.
summary: Yahoo Finance reports that the S&P 500, the index of large US companies, is up about 13.5% this year, but an index that removes AI-related names has gained only 5.5%, against about 5.6% for Europe's STOXX 600 index. BNP Paribas economists say Europe has probably missed out on the AI investment boom, though the article adds that the US was already ahead before ChatGPT, that AI has widened the gap rather than created it, and that, per Goldman Sachs, the US and Canada hold about 60% of new data-centre capacity added in 2026 against Europe's roughly 10%.
notes: Read in full. Yahoo Finance's own reporter (Jake Conley); disclosure in the article about Apollo Global Management, whose data is cited.
